- The board is \(10\) grid units wide and \(8\) units high. Point \(P\) is \(4\) units from the left edge, so it is \(6\) units from the right edge.
- Since
  \[
  \tan\theta=\frac{\text{vertical rise}}{\text{horizontal run}}=\frac12,
  \]
  the ball’s direction is proportional to \((2,1)\).
- Traveling \(6\) units right from \(P\), the ball rises \(3\) units and hits the right side.
- Reflection at the vertical side reverses the horizontal component, giving direction \((-2,1)\).
- From that impact point, the upper-left corner \(C\) is \(10\) units left and \(5\) units up. This displacement is
  \[
  (-10,5)=5(-2,1),
  \]
  exactly the reflected direction.

Therefore, the ball reaches the upper-left corner.
